criteria.criterion: Evidence-backed height, floors, and roof form
evidence: Saved bounds reach 16.96 m; eaves and roof heights are explicitly estimates, not measurements.
Historic 1960–62 and 2006 construction-stage photographs support steep intersecting roofs, dormers, chimneys, and gable cues.

The saved render has a tall, steep main roof, two dormers, and chimneys, but the dominant uninterrupted roof plane does not reproduce the more articulated intersecting gable roof visible in source photographs.
Floor count remains unverified; available GIS level fields are unreliable/conflicting evidence.
findings: No elevation or point-cloud source establishes height or floor count. Roof massing is only partly matched: subdivide the long roof plane with the photo-supported intersecting cross-gables and roof breaks.

evidence: Photo sources show Tudor Revival, rough masonry/stucco, prominent cross-gables, an arched opening, a substantial timbered entrance, and irregularly grouped openings.
The model now includes a visible gabled entry porch, divided windows, trim, dormers, chimney stacks, and an L-shaped shell.

Rendered facades remain mostly uniform flat wall courses with evenly repeated rectangular windows; stone/masonry articulation, arched feature, timbering and historic entrance proportions are weak or absent.
findings: Photo-backed identity cues improved, but signature Tudor features and facade composition are not well reproduced. Add the photo-supported entry timber framing/stone surround, arched gable opening, and irregular window groupings.
